## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The arbitrary-level Murphy basis and higher ideals of
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]], and the
ordinary Jucys–Murphy triangularity
([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]]).

[F1] The Murphy elements $m_{st}$ form a dominance-cellular basis with higher
two-sided ideals $N^{>\lambda}$, and
$m_\lambda(X_{a+1}-Q_k)=x_\lambda u_b\in N^{>\lambda}$ for $a=a_k$
([[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]]); the
generators satisfy
$T_iX_i=X_{i+1}T_i-(q_H-1)X_{i+1}$ and
$T_iX_{i+1}=X_iT_i+(q_H-1)X_{i+1}$, with distant commutation
([[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]]).

[F2] The ordinary multiplicative Jucys–Murphy elements
$M_i=q_H^{1-i}T_{i-1}\cdots T_1^2\cdots T_{i-1}=1+(q_H-1)L_i$ act on ordinary
standard tableaux with diagonal $q_H^{\mathrm{content}}$
([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The multipartition $\lambda$, the Murphy module $S_\lambda$ with its

basis $m_t$, and the data of [F1]–[F2].

1.1 Initial-row eigenvalues. For component $k$ and $a=a_k$, [F1] gives $m_\lambda(X_{a+1}-Q_k)=x_\lambda u_b\in N^{>\lambda}$. The internal finite Hecke submodule generated by $m_\lambda$ modulo higher global shapes is spanned by standard internal component permutations; each such permutation fixes the smallest internal label $a+1$ (that label occupies the first node of its component), so its Hecke element has a reduced word in the internal generators with indices at least $a+2$ and commutes with $X_{a+1}$. Hence $X_{a+1}$ acts as the scalar $Q_k$ on that whole submodule, with errors in the two-sided ideal $N^{>\lambda}$. The $X$-recurrence then identifies $X_{a+i}$ on this submodule with $Q_k$ times the ordinary multiplicative Jucys–Murphy element $M_i$ of [F2], by induction from the finite quadratic relation and the additive-JM recurrence (a polynomial identity also at $q_H=1$). Ordinary JM triangularity gives diagonal $Q_kq_H^{c-r}$ at the node $(r,c,k)$ occupied by local entry $i$: the internal label $i$ is not a row index, and no extra subtraction of $i-1$ occurs. For the initial component tableau, which is maximal in tableau dominance, there are no strictly more dominant same-shape terms. Thus for the node $(r,c,k)$ carrying global entry $t$, $m_\lambda X_t\equiv Q_kq_H^{c-r}m_\lambda\pmod{N^{>\lambda}}$.  [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 JM triangularity for every standard multitableau. Inducting through a reduced word of $w$, the relations [F1] give $T_wX_r=X_{w^{-1}(r)}T_w+\sum_{v<w}\sum_ba_{(v,b)}X_bT_v,$ where the corrections are supported on proper Bruhat subwords (at the first correction a generator is deleted, moving its linear $X$-coefficient through preceding generators deletes further generators, and finite quadratic multiplication preserves Bruhat support). Applying this with $w=d(t)$ and multiplying by $m_\lambda$ on the left, step 1.1 evaluates every surviving $X$ coefficient modulo higher shapes; a correction $m_\lambda T_v$ reduces first to a row-standard representative $d(u)$ of its Young-subgroup coset, the removed row subgroup contributing its row eigenvalue, with $d(u)\le v<d(t)$; the Bruhat/tableau-prefix relation on the ordered rows of all components then makes $u$ strictly dominate $t$, and componentwise straightening of $u$ keeps the shape or produces same-shape tableaux at least $u$ in prefix dominance, hence strictly dominating $t$. The leading eigenvalue is $Q_kq_H^{j-i}$ at the node carrying $r$, because $w^{-1}(r)$ is its initial-row label. Therefore $m_{(t^\lambda,t)}X_r\equiv Q_kq_H^{j-i}m_{(t^\lambda,t)} +\sum_{v\lhd t}a_vm_{(t^\lambda,v)}\pmod{N^{>\lambda}},$ the exact arbitrary-level JM content statement, independent of an affine center theorem, semisimplicity or block classification. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Residue words and boundary cases. On the resulting Specht module a total ordering extending tableau dominance triangularizes all the $X_r$ simultaneously; the one-dimensional successive quotients have exactly the content characters of step 2.1, so every simultaneous generalized eigenword is among the standard-tableau residue words $c_a+j-i\pmod e$ ([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]] for the ordinary part); the residue multiplicities of every such word equal the node-residue multiplicities of $\lambda$, since permuting the labels of a standard tableau does not change the multiset of node residues. For rank zero, $H=F$, the sole shape and tableau are empty and all assertions have their one-dimensional interpretation. The triangularity is polynomial in the parameters, so it specializes to the LM deformation DVR and to the generic fibre. [step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

The lemma supplies the content-triangularity input of the Jantzen and
core-reduction theory over the original parameters, with no semisimplicity or
affine-center hypothesis; the diagonal is the node content and the corrections
are strictly dominant standard tableaux.

their intrinsic standards, and the actual local and categorical suppliers
below.

[F1] Generic support is finite in each rank, with colors within $d-1$ of a
charge, and the two integer-color local inverse tables glue to actual
word-preserving tower maps and residue bimodules
([[lem-generic-cyclotomic-type-a-support-is-bounded-by-rank]],
[[lem-integer-color-degenerate-hecke-klr-local-inverse-tables]],
[[lem-generic-nondegenerate-local-inverse-tables]],
[[lem-generic-cyclotomic-local-dictionaries-glue-to-a-tower]]).

act on the cell basis with dominance-triangular diagonal
$U_jz^{c-r}$ at node $(r,c,j)$
([[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]],
[[lem-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-murphy-jm-action-is-content-triangular]]).
This is a universal parameter identity, not an invocation of a finite-$e$

[F3] The actual Schur standard is affine induction of evaluated ordinary
complex Spechts; its affine action factors through the cyclotomic quotient
([[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]]).
The affine PBW basis and evaluation $x_r\mapsto m+J_r$ are proved in
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]], and the ordinary Specht joint

[F4] The actual degenerate $K_0$ and $G_0$ identifications give the full lower
and upper integral lattices, normalized cover/simple families, Chevalley and
divided-power operators and all compatible finite cuts
([[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-projective-k-zero-is-the-highest-weight-module]],
[[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]],

([[thm-split-simple-projective-hom-pairing-has-dual-bases]]).

**Proof technique:** direct.

Thus the proved affine inverse dictionaries descend in both directions to the same homogeneous cyclotomic KLR presentation. Their inverse composites fix words, dots and crossings, with the prescribed right-side order of their series. This gives the actual maps $\phi_d^{\deg},\phi_d^\xi$ and hence $\Theta_d$; no arbitrary rankwise isomorphism is selected. Their local series are independent of rank, charge order and window. The prefix projector is the sum over its appended colors, so the tower maps agree; the common last-color idempotent identifies the two induction bimodules by $a\epsilon_i\otimes v\mapsto\Theta_{d+1}(a)\epsilon_i\otimes v$, and identifies the restrictions. In a fixed finite rank bound every series is a finite nilpotent Taylor sum; window enlargement adds only zero unsupported words. Therefore the comparison preserves actual word projectors, residue functors and their finite compositions. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

An idempotent image is an exact functor, so both characters are additive and descend to $G_0$. Infinite order makes $\nu\mapsto(\xi^{\nu_1},\ldots,\xi^{\nu_d})$ injective.
